$\int_0^\pi\left[\cos ^2\left(\frac{3 \pi}{8}-\frac{x}{4}\right)-\cos ^2\left(\frac{11 \pi}{8}+\frac{x}{4}\right)\right] d x$
equals to
questions.solution: $I=\int_0^\pi\left[\cos ^2\left(\frac{3 \pi}{8}-\frac{x}{4}\right)-\cos ^2\left(\frac{11 \pi}{8}+\frac{x}{4}\right)\right] d x\begin{aligned} & =\int_0^\pi\left[\cos ^2\left(\frac{3 \pi}{8}-\frac{x}{4}\right)-\cos ^2\left(\pi+\left(\frac{3 \pi}{8}+\frac{x}{4}\right)\right] d x\right. \\ & =\int_0^\pi\left[\cos ^2\left(\frac{3 \pi}{8}-\frac{x}{4}\right)-\cos ^2\left(\frac{3 \pi}{8}+\frac{x}{4}\right)\right] d x\end{aligned}=\int_0^\pi\left[\begin{array}{r}\cos\left(\frac{3 \pi}{8}-\frac{x}{4}+\frac{3 \pi}{8}+\frac{x}{4}\right) \\ \cdot \cos\left(\frac{3 \pi}{8}-\frac{x}{4}-\frac{3 \pi}{8}-\frac{x}{4}\right)\end{array}\right]\begin{aligned} & =\int_0^\pi \cos \left(\frac{3 \pi}{4}\right) \cdot \cos \left(-\frac{x}{2}\right) \cdot d x \\ & =-\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \int_0^\pi \cos \left(\frac{-x}{2}\right) d x\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} \text{ Let }-\frac{x}{2} & =t \Rightarrow d x=-2 d t \\ & =-\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \int_0^{\frac{\pi}{2}}-2 \cos t \cdot d t \\ & =\frac{2}{\sqrt{2}} \int_0^{\frac{\pi}{2}} \cos t \cdot d t \\ & =\sqrt{2}[\sin t]_0^{\frac{\pi}{2}}=\sqrt{2}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: The value of the integral $\int_{-1}^{3}(|x|+|x-1|) d x$ is
questions.solution:
We have
$$
|x|+|x-1|=\left\{\begin{array}{c}
-x-(x-1)=-2 x+1, \text{ if } x \leq 0 \\
x-(x-1)=1, \text{ if } 0 \leq x \leq 1 \\
x+x-1=2 x-1, \text{ if } x \geq 1
\end{array}\right.
$$
$$
\begin{aligned}
& \therefore \int_{-1}^{3}(|x|+|x-1|) d x \\
=& \int_{-1}^{0}(-2 x+1) d x+\int_{0}^{1} 1 d x+\int_{1}^{3}(2 x-1) d x \\
=&\left[-x^{2}+x\right]_{-1}^{0}+[x]_{0}^{1}+\left[x^{2}-x\right]_{1}^{3}=9
\end{aligned}
$$

questions.q:
If \(f^{\prime}(x)=f(x)+\int_0^1 f(x) d x\) and given \(f(0)=1\).
Then \(f(x)=\)
questions.solution:
Given \(f^{\prime}(x)=f(x)+\int_0^1 f(x) d x\) ...(1)
Differentiating we get,
\(f^{\prime \prime}(x)=f^{\prime}(x)+0 \Rightarrow \frac{f^{\prime \prime}(x)}{f^{\prime}(x)}=1\)
On integrating \(\int \frac{f^{\prime \prime}(x)}{f^{\prime}(x)} d x=\int d x\)
\(\Rightarrow \ln f^{\prime}(x)=x+c \Rightarrow f^{\prime}(x)=e^{x+c}=k e^x\)
where \(\mathrm{k}=\mathrm{e}^{\mathrm{c}}\), a constant
Again integrate
\(\int f^{\prime}(x) d x=\int k e^x+D \Rightarrow f(x)=k e^x+D\) ...(2)
Put \(x=0\) in (1), \(f(0)=\mathrm{ke}^{\circ}+\mathrm{D} \Rightarrow \mathrm{k}+\mathrm{D}=1\)
(given \(f(0)=1)\) ...(3)
Also from (1), \(f^{\prime}(x)=f(x)+\int_0^1 f(x) d x\)
\(\begin{aligned}
& \Rightarrow \mathrm{ke}^{\mathrm{x}}=\mathrm{ke}^{\mathrm{x}}+\mathrm{D}+\int_0^1\left(\mathrm{ke}^{\mathrm{x}}+\mathrm{D}\right) \mathrm{dx} \\
& \Rightarrow\left[\mathrm{ke}^{\mathrm{x}}+\mathrm{Dx}\right]_0^1+\mathrm{D}=0 \Rightarrow[\mathrm{ke}+\mathrm{D}-\mathrm{k}]+\mathrm{D}=0 \\
& \Rightarrow \mathrm{k}(\mathrm{e}-1)+2 \mathrm{D}=0
\end{aligned}\)
Solving (3) and (4), we get
\(\begin{aligned}
& \mathrm{k}=\frac{2}{3-\mathrm{e}} \text{ and } \mathrm{D}=\frac{1-\mathrm{e}}{3-\mathrm{e}} \\
& \therefore \mathrm{f}(\mathrm{x})=\frac{2 \mathrm{e}^{\mathrm{x}}}{3-\mathrm{e}}+\frac{1-\mathrm{e}}{3-\mathrm{e}}
\end{aligned}\)

Now, put \mathrm{n}=2$ in equation $(2)$, we get $g(x)=1 \$pmx^{2} \begin{aligned}

&=1 \pm9=10,-8
\end{aligned}$

questions.q: $\int_{0}^{2 x}(\sin x+|\sin x|) d x$ is equal to
questions.solution: $\int_{0}^{2 \pi}(\sin x+|\sin x|) d x=\int_{0}^{\pi}(\sin x+\sin x) d x+\quad \int_{\pi}^{2 \pi}(\sin x-\sin x) d x=2 \int_{0}^{\pi} \sin x d x+0=-2 \int_{0}^{\pi} \cos x d x=-2(\cos \pi-\cos 0)=-2(-1-1)=4$

questions.q: Find the number of ways in which five large books, four medium-size books, and three small books can be placed on a shelf so that all books of the same size are together.
questions.solution:
Let us make one packet for each of the books on the same size. Now, 3 packets can be arranged in $\mathrm{P}(3,3)=3 !$ ways 5 large books can be arranged in $5 !$ ways 4 medium size books can be arranged in $4 !$ ways
3 small books can be arranged in $3 !$ ways
$\therefore$ Required number of ways $=3 ! \times 5 ! \times 4 ! \times 3 !$ ways

questions.q: Consider the set $\mathrm{Q}$ of rational numbers. Let $*$ be the operation on $Q$ defined by $a * b=a+b-a b$. The identity element under $*$ is
questions.solution:
An identity relation is one in which every element of a set is related to itself only. $\mathbf{a} * \mathbf{b}=\mathbf{a}+\mathbf{b}-\mathbf{a b}$
As in identity relation ' $a$ ' is related to 'a', so the correct option will be the one which gives the value of the relation $=$ 'a'. So, equating $a+b-a b=a$, we get $b(1-a)=0$ Now putting the values of $a$, we find $b$ and the option in which $\mathrm{a}=\mathrm{b}$, will be the answer. For $a=0, b=0$, so the correct option.
For $a=1, b(1-1)=0 \Rightarrow b$ can have multiple values.
For $\mathrm{a}=2, \mathrm{ b}(1-2)=0 \Rightarrow \mathrm{b}=0$ but $\mathrm{a}=2$

questions.q: If $\mathrm{B}$ is a non-singular matrix and $\mathrm{A}$ is a square matrix, then $\operatorname\det  \left(\mathrmB^{-1} \mathrm{AB}\right) is equal to$
questions.solution:
$\begin{array}{l}
 $\operatorname{det}$\left(B^{-1} A B\right)$=\operatorname{det}$\left(B^{-1}\right) \operatorname{det} A \operatorname{det}$ B \\
=$\operatorname{det}\left(B^{-1}\right)$ \cdot $\operatorname{det}$B \cdot $\operatorname{det}A \\
=$\operatorname{det}$\left(B^{-1} B\right)\operatorname{det} A=$\operatorname{det}$ I \cdot $\operatorname{det}A \\
=1 \cdot $\operatorname{det}A=$\operatorname{det}$ A
\end{array}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Let $\mathrm{A}$ and $\mathrm{B}$ are two fixed points in a plane then locus of another point $C$ on the same plane such that $\mathrm{CA}+\mathrm{CB}=$ constant,$( > \mathrm{AB})$ is
questions.solution:
Let two fixed points be $\mathrm{A}(\mathrm{ae}, 0)$ and $\mathrm{B}(-\mathrm{ae},$, $0)$. Let $\mathrm{C}(\mathrm{x}, \mathrm{y})$ be a moving point such that $\mathrm{AC}+\mathrm{CB}=$ constant $=2 \mathrm{a}$ (say)
i.e., $\sqrt{(x-a e)^{2}+(y-0)^{2}} +\sqrt{(x+a e)^{2}+(y-0)^{2}}=2 a \text{$ Or $} \sqrt{x^{2}+y^{2}+a^{2} e^{2}-2 a e x} +\sqrt{x^{2}+y^{2}+a^{2} e^{2}+2 a e x}=2 a$ ...(1)
Or $l+\mathrm{m}=2 \mathrm{a}$ ...(2)
Where, $l^{2}=\mathrm{x}^{2}+\mathrm{y}^{2}+\mathrm{a}^{2} \mathrm{e}^{2}-2 \mathrm{aex}$ ...(3)
and $m^{2}=x^{2}+y^{2}+a^{2} e^{2}+2 a e x$ ...(4)
From, (3) and (4)
$\begin{array}{l}
\quad \mathrm{m}^{2}-l^{2}=4 \mathrm{aex} \\
\text{ or } \quad(\mathrm{m}-l)(l+\mathrm{m})=4 \mathrm{aex} \\
2 \mathrm{a}(\mathrm{m}-l)=4 \mathrm{aex} \quad[\text{ From }(2)] \\
\mathrm{m}-l=2 \mathrm{ex} ...(5)
\end{array}$
Adding $(2) and (5)$, we get
$\mathrm{m}=\mathrm{a}+\mathrm{ex}$ ...(6)
From (4) and (6),
$\begin{array}{l}
\mathrm{a}^{2}+\mathrm{e}^{2}\mathrm{x}^{2}+2 \mathrm{aex}=\mathrm{x}^{2}+\mathrm{y}^{2}+\mathrm{a}^{2}\mathrm{e}^{2}+2 \mathrm{aex} \\
\Rightarrow \quad \mathrm{x}^{2}\left(1-\mathrm{e}^{2}$\right)$+\mathrm{y}^{2}=\mathrm{a}^{2}\left(1-\mathrm{e}^{2}\right)$
\end{array}$
Dividing both sides by \mathrm{a}^{2}\left(1-\mathrm{e}^{2}\right)$, we get
$\frac{x^{2}}{a^{2}}+\frac{y^{2}}{a^{2}\left(1-e^{2}\right)$}=1 Or $\frac{x^{2}}{a^{2}}+\frac{y^{2}}{b^{2}}=1$, where $b^{2}=a^{2}\left(1-e^{2}\right)
This is$ the equation of ellipse.
